features.name: Portable machines
features.what: Small, light machines with a case, for travel and the home.

features.name: Ink ribbon
features.what: An inked fabric ribbon between the type and the paper, in place of ink pads and rollers.
features.today: Typewriters to the end; impact and receipt printers still use ribbons.

features.name: Space bar
features.what: One long bar under the keys that moves the carriage one space without printing.

features.name: Line-end bell
features.what: A bell that rings a few characters before the right margin.

features.name: Proportional spacing
features.what: Each letter takes a space to suit its width (m wide, i narrow) instead of one fixed pitch; IBM's Executive (1944) brought it to offices.
features.today: Proportional fonts: nearly all text today.

features.name: Correction and erasing
features.what: Ways to remove or cover a mistake: erasing tables and shields, then (after 1950) correcting ribbons.

features.name: Shift key (case shift)
features.what: Two characters on each type bar or row, and a key that shifts the carriage or the type basket so the second one prints: half the keys for the same character set.

features.name: Automatic ribbon reverse
features.what: The ribbon spools change direction by themselves when one runs empty.

features.name: Carriage return and line space
features.what: One lever that turns the platen to the next line and pushes the carriage back to the start.
features.today: The Return or Enter key; CR and LF in character codes (ASCII, 1963).

features.name: Interchangeable type
features.what: A type wheel, shuttle or sleeve that lifts out, so one machine writes in several typefaces or languages.
features.today: Changeable fonts: the Selectric's golf ball (1961), daisy wheels, then digital fonts.

features.name: Margin stops and release
features.what: Adjustable stops for the left and right margins, and a key to type past them.

features.name: Electric drive
features.what: A motor or magnets do the work of the type stroke and carriage, so a light touch prints evenly.
features.today: Electric and electronic typewriters, then computer keyboards.

features.name: Tabulator
features.what: Stops set along the carriage and a key that runs the carriage to the next one, for columns and indents.
features.today: The Tab key and tab stops (HT in ASCII).

features.name: Shift lock
features.what: Holds the shift down for a run of capitals.

features.name: QWERTY keyboard
features.what: The Sholes and Glidden layout, which Remington's success made the norm; rivals such as the Ideal (DHIATENSOR) layout lost out.
features.today: Still the standard layout of computer and phone keyboards.

features.name: Visible writing
features.what: Type that strikes the front of the platen, so the typist sees the line as it is written; on early understrike machines the writing was hidden until the carriage was lifted.
features.today: Seeing the text as you type, on every later typewriter and every screen.

features.name: Backspace
features.what: A key that moves the carriage back one space, to correct or to overstrike.

features.name: Two-colour ribbon
features.what: A ribbon with two bands (usually black and red) and a lever that lifts the ribbon to print in the second colour.

features.name: Decimal tabulator
features.what: A row of tab keys for units, tens, hundreds and so on, so figures line up on the decimal point.
features.today: Decimal tab stops in word processors.
